public_rationale: Zitron hypothesized that if OpenAI survived more than two years, it would have had to raise more than any startup ever had, and keep raising at an unseen pace. OpenAI was still operating in September 2026, so the condition is met (e1). After the post, OpenAI closed a $40B round in March 2025, which PitchBook data put at nearly three times the previous private tech record (e2). Less than a year later it closed a $110B round, then reported as $122B, again the largest private tech financing ever (e3, e4), and by September 2026 it was in talks for more. So what he said survival would take did happen. This grade does not show that record fundraising was strictly necessary. It shows only that survival and the named condition happened together.
limitations: Necessity cannot be proved, only co-occurrence.
The speaker framed this as a hypothesis.
Relies on news reports of announced round sizes, not audited figures.

our_interpretation: This is a necessary-condition hypothesis: if OpenAI survives more than two years after the post, it will have done so by raising record sums. The part that can be checked is whether both happened: OpenAI still operating after 2026-07-29, and record-setting fundraising after the post.
The two-year mark is only used to check the condition (survival). It is not treated as a deadline for the fundraising. Funding events up to the evaluation date count.

'More money than any startup has ever raised' is read as a single private funding round, or a cumulative total, larger than any private company had raised before. 'A pace totally unseen' is read as more record-scale raises following within a short time.

Whether record fundraising was strictly necessary for survival is a counterfactual and cannot be proved. The grade covers only whether the condition he named came true alongside survival. The hedge 'I am hypothesizing' is kept in the flags.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI is operating after 2026-07-29, and after the post it raised a funding round or total larger than any startup had ever raised, followed by more record-scale raises.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI is operating after 2026-07-29 but got there without record fundraising, for example by funding itself from revenue or ordinary-sized rounds.
